profile.summary: Optimus 5-Prime is a convolutional neural network that predicts how well a 5' UTR sequence drives translation, measured as mean ribosome load (MRL). It reads a one-hot encoded 5' UTR, 50 nucleotides in the main model, and outputs a single MRL value. It was trained on polysome profiling of 280,000 random 5' UTRs placed in front of an eGFP reporter, and the authors also used it with a genetic algorithm to design new 5' UTRs.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; Results, Modeling 5' UTRs and ribosome loading; Fig. 2 legend

summary_quotes.text: that could quantitatively capture the relationship between 5′ UTR sequences and their associated MRLs
Optimus 5-Prime structure: A one-hot encoded 5′ UTR sequence is fed into a CNN composed of three convolution layers and a fully connected layer to produce a linear output predicting MRL.
we combine polysome profiling of a library of 280,000 randomized 5′ UTRs with deep learning to build a predictive model that relates human 5′ UTR sequence to translation
Together with a genetic algorithm, we use the model to engineer new 5′ UTRs

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The authors built a library of 280,000 reporter constructs with random 5' UTRs and a constant eGFP coding sequence and 3' UTR, measured ribosome loading by polysome profiling and RNA sequencing, and trained a CNN on 260,000 of them, holding out 20,000 for testing. The chosen architecture, from a 10-fold cross-validated grid search, has three convolution layers of 120 filters with filter length 8 and ReLU activation, a 40-node dense layer with 20% dropout, and one linear output. It was written in Python 2.7 with Keras on a TensorFlow backend and trained for three epochs. A separate model with the same layout predicts the full polysome profile, and a generalised version reads 5' UTRs of 25 to 100 nucleotides, zero-padded to 100.

we trained a convolutional neural network (CNN) with 260,000 of the 280,000-member eGFP library. The remaining 20,000 sequences were withheld for testing.

The input space was expanded to 100 nucleotides using one-hot encoding; for sequences shorter than 100 nt zero padding was used.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The repository holds several saved Keras models in modeling/saved_models: the main MRL model (Figure 2), a retrained main model (Figure 4), a model for the genetic algorithm and its retrained version, and the polysome distribution model. The same folder also holds Varying_length_25to100_model.hdf5, whose name matches the paper's generalised 25 to 100 nucleotide model. Six further .h5 models (e1, e2, ep1, ep2, emp1, emp2) sit in modeling/cds_modification_comparisons/saved_data; the paper describes models trained on chemically modified RNA, but the sources read do not explain these file names. A result should name the saved .hdf5 file and the commit; this page read commit d53df410. Training data are on GEO (GSE114002).

strengths.text: The authors report that the main model explained 93% of MRL variation on 20,000 held-out random UTRs, against at best 66% for position-specific k-mer linear models.
strengths.source_locator: Paper: Modeling 5' UTRs and ribosome loading

quotes.text: Optimus 5-Prime could explain 93% of MRL variation in the test set
position-specific k-mer (k = 1–6) linear models could at best explain 66% of the variation in the test set

strengths.text: Models are also trained for chemically modified mRNA (pseudouridine and 1-methyl-pseudouridine), which matters for mRNA therapeutics.
strengths.source_locator: Paper: Abstract; Evaluation of mRNA containing pseudouridine

quotes.text: We show that the same approach can be extended to chemically modified RNA, an important feature for applications in mRNA therapeutics and synthetic biology.

strengths.text: Usable for sequence design: the model was paired with a genetic algorithm to evolve 5' UTRs towards a target ribosome load.

limitations.text: Fixed input length: the main model reads only 50 nucleotides, covering 13% of human 5' UTRs; the generalised model reaches 100 nucleotides (29%). Human 5' UTRs have a median length of 218 nt.

review.note: Written from the human_5utr_modeling README, LICENSE, modeling/saved_models/README and human_5utrs/human_utr_modeling.ipynb and the GitHub tree listing at commit d53df410, and the NCBI author manuscript of Sample et al. 2019 (PMC7100133), each fetched on 2026-11-26. No command was executed and no human review is claimed.

no_run_guide_reason: The README gives no install or run commands, only a note to create a 'data' folder and place the GEO CSV files in it. The models are used from Python 2 Jupyter notebooks with unpinned Keras and TensorFlow versions, so a runnable sequence of commands cannot be written without inventing steps.
notes: The existing FramePool 2021 sources were not read or cited; the fixed-length limitation is taken from the model's own paper. Europe PMC returned HTTP 500 twice for PMC7100133, so the NCBI efetch copy of the author manuscript was used.
